title: Noisy Dependency Correlation and Alert Debouncing — SRE Notes
content:
Summary:

This is a working record of recurring noisy alerts in the last three weeks tied to upstream dependency latency spikes. Symptoms: repeated SLO-burn alerts for hosted-api-route-50x-rate and api-request-latency-p90 firing in quick succession, followed by large waves of PagerDuty pages even though user-visible error rates were intermittent. On-call teams observed flapping between 'sustained SLO burn' and 'return-to-normal' within 10–20 minutes repeatedly.

Why this is different from past noise problems:
- The root signal is a transient lag in a downstream dependency (third-party auth service and a caching layer) that manifests as more retries and longer tails in request latency distribution.
- Current alerts use short evaluation windows (1m/5m) and simple thresholds; that allowed multiple alerts to fire for the same underlying incident as metric aggregates drifted in and out of thresholds.
- Alert grouping is by top-level service only; different endpoints with different retry behavior create multiple alert streams and duplicate pages.

Timeline (high level):
- 2025-02-03: first spike observed during evening deploys; noisy pages, manual mutes applied.
- 2025-02-18: repeat incident, hypothesis formed that dependency X throttles at ~2000rps causing connection queuing.
- 2025-02-25: synthetic tests show 200–300ms tail latency increase on auth calls when load >70th percentile.
- 2025-03-01: introduced temporary Alertmanager route to group alerts by incident_key; mitigated pages but not root churn.

Signals and queries used during triage (examples):
- PromQL (request latency tail):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service, endpoint))

- PromQL (SLO burn rate):
  sum(rate(slo_error_count_total[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(slo_total_requests[5m])) by (service)

- BigQuery (ingested logs) example to find retry storms:
  SELECT timestamp, request_path, status_code, reties_count
  FROM `redwood-logging.prod_http_requests`
  WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
  AND service = 'hosted-api'
  ORDER BY reties_count DESC
  LIMIT 200;

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Dependency throttling + exponential backoff jitter amplifies tail latencies and causes bursty retry storms that briefly spike error counts.
2) Alert evaluation windows too short; alerts are reactive to sampling noise instead of sustained degradation.
3) Alert routing groups by service only, leading to parallel alert streams for each affected endpoint, increasing page volume.
4) Metrics ingestion lag (prometheus scrape lag of up to ~30s during high cardinality) makes 1m alerts unstable.

Immediate mitigations (what on-call did this week):
- Temporarily increased alert evaluation to 5m for the top-level SLO alerts (quick change in Alertmanager) — reduced duplicate pages.
- Applied a 10-minute manual suppression for non-critical SLOs during the largest spike to prevent escalation while debugging.
- Escalated to dependency owner; they confirmed a throttling change in their infra around the same window.

Proposed debouncing rules (draft):
- Debounce layer 1 (noise suppression): require alert condition to be true for 3/5 evaluation buckets (5m windows with 1m step) before creating a page.
- Debounce layer 2 (dependency correlation): if downstream-dependency-latency > 95th (5m) for same time window, group related SLO alerts under a single incident_key and route to one escalation policy.
- Debounce layer 3 (global outage detection): if >50% of endpoints for a service report concurrent SLO burn, escalate immediately (no debounce).

Alert and routing changes to implement (actionable):
1) Change firing rules for api-request-latency-p90 and hosted-api-route-50x-rate to use a rolling 5m evaluation and require sustained condition (3/5). (Owner: eng-sre)
2) Add an Alertmanager matcher that attaches dependency tags (dependency=auth-service, dependency=kv-cache) using relabeling from the scrape job. (Owner: observability team)
3) Create suppression rules for non-production namespaces and low-traffic endpoints to avoid waking on-call for minor fluctuations. (Owner: eng-sre & product)
4) Add an aggregation endpoint in Alertmanager to collapse alerts with the same incident_key and present a single aggregated notification. (Owner: infra-alerting)

Runbook (operational steps for on-call):
- Triage checklist:
  1) Check global incident board (incidents.redwood.io) for existing incident_key. If present, add notes and silence individual alerts, do not open new incident.
  2) Query dependency latency: run the PromQL snippet for dependency_http_request_duration_seconds by (dependency). Identify if any dependency shows 95th > baseline + 200ms.
  3) Examine logs for retry counts (BigQuery snippet above). If retries_count > 2 for >5% of requests, assume retry storm.
  4) If retry storm present, temporarily mute per-endpoint SLO alerts and open a consolidated incident.
  5) If no dependency signal, treat as service-only regression and follow SLO escalation path.

Commands and playbook snippets:
- Mute route in Alertmanager (example):
  curl -XPOST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n   https://alertmanager.internal/api/v1/silences \n   -d '{"matchers":[{"name":"alertname","value":"api-request-latency-p90"}],"startsAt":"2025-03-07T15:00:00Z","endsAt":"2025-03-07T15:30:00Z","createdBy":"oncall","comment":"temporary debounce during investigation"}'

- Identify top endpoints causing SLO burn (PromQL):
  topk(10, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_count[5m])) by (endpoint, service) * histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint)))

Telemetry improvements (follow-ups):
- Add a derived metric: dependency_retry_storm_indicator{service, dependency} = increase(retries_total[5m]) / increase(requests_total[5m]) — expose as a ratio and use as an alert input.
- Reduce Prometheus scrape cardinality for high-cardinality labels (request_id) during high QPS paths; move those labels to logs, not metrics.
- Add latency-weighted SLO burn metric so single long-tail requests don't produce disproportionate alerts.

Planned experiments (scheduling):
1) Synthetic replay: run controlled replay of recorded traffic against staging with dependency delays injected (+100ms, +300ms, +600ms) to observe alerting behavior and confirm debounce thresholds. (Owner: applied-ml infra test team)
2) Blackbox test: schedule hourly synthetic auth checks from multiple regions to detect dependency tail latency early. (Owner: infra)
3) A/B alerting: rollout new debounce rules to 10% of alerts (staged Alertmanager route) and measure page volume, MTTA, and MTTR over 2 weeks. (Owner: observability)

Acceptance criteria for rollout:
- Page volume for incidents driven by dependency latency should drop >= 60% without increasing time-to-detect by >50%.
- No missed major incidents: when synthetic injection shows >1% error rate sustained for 10m, a page must still be generated.
- Engineers report lower cognitive load during morning handoffs for two consecutive weeks.

Open questions / risks:
- Debouncing increases time-to-alert for genuine regressions; need careful threshold tuning and good synthetic coverage.
- Attaching dependency tags requires changes to metric relabeling; risk of losing label fidelity.
- Some services have heterogeneous endpoints where per-endpoint debouncing may hide real regressions.

Next steps (short term):
- Implement a 5m rolling evaluation change for the top SLO alerts (eng-sre, due 2025-03-14).
- Add dependency retry ratio metric to the observability backlog and prioritize for Q2.
- Run the synthetic replay job in staging this quarter and capture alert behaviors.

Notes to self: Keep updates short in incident summaries; prefer "consolidated incident" over multiple PD pages. Consider adding a tiny Jupyter notebook that simulates debounce thresholds on historical alerts to choose parameters empirically.

Appendix: useful links and references
- Incident timeline GSheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example
- Related Linear: INF-8923, INF-9021
- PR for temporary Alertmanager route: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/412

End of note.
